axes.label: Craft & polish
axes.description: Visual quality, typography, colour, composition, motion feel, finish. Would a discerning person believe a human designed this on purpose?

axes.label: Technical ambition
axes.description: How hard is what was actually built, and is it built correctly? Real technique versus the cheapest thing that looks similar.

axes.label: Brief adherence
axes.description: Did it do everything the prompt asked, completely, including the output contract? Stubs and TODOs count against.

axes.label: Originality
axes.description: Is the idea and its execution distinctive, or is it the median AI answer to this prompt?

redFlags: Four lights (hemisphere, directional, two point lights) are added and their intensities animated per frame, but every material in the scene is a raw ShaderMaterial with hand-written lighting — the 'meaningful lighting' is dead code that has no effect on the render.
Ring vertex shader declares `attribute float alpha` that is never supplied by the geometry (unused/dead declaration).
Small per-frame allocations (two new THREE.Vector3 in the render loop) against the brief's 'no allocating per frame'.

The brief specifies that scroll is the only timeline, but uTime continuously drives star twinkling, nebula drift, planet displacement, terrain waves/sparkles, mote movement, rotations, and exposure independently of scroll.

IcosahedronGeometry is requested with detail 14, an unnecessarily extreme subdivision setting that risks very large initialization/memory cost depending on Three.js's internal detail cap; it is disproportionate to the visible result.
Landing chapter text opacity is 0 at scroll progress 0 by construction of updateText.
Advertised 'dispersion' and 'thin-film iridescence' are decorative hacks (a channel offset and a sin of dot(n,vec3(1))) that produce no visible effect in the shipped render.
The meta panel prints 'WEBGL2' unconditionally; if the WebGL1 fallback path is taken the #version 300 es shader cannot compile and the page degrades to an error string in the fallback copy.

The WebGL1 fallback attempt cannot compile the WebGL2 `#version 300 es` shaders; it does subsequently show the considered fallback message, so this is graceful but the WebGL1 context acquisition is effectively unnecessary.
`u_dpr` is declared, located, and updated but never used by the shader.
The shader's advertised “refraction” is an environment-direction approximation rather than physically propagated/transmitted glass, though the code itself labels it as fake.

Hero reveal elements ship with class="reveal in" already applied, so the staggered transition-delay values are dead code — there is no entrance animation on first paint, only on scroll for later sections.

Duplicate style attribute on the brass swatch label (`style="position:absolute…" class="mono" style="font-size:.58rem;background:…"`) means the second declaration is dropped and the "01 — Brass" chip renders without its frame.

Inline `style="grid-column:1/7"` on the hero copy overrides the `@media(max-width:900px){.hero-copy{grid-column:auto}}` rule, so the mobile hero relies on implicit column generation rather than the stacked layout the CSS intends; anchor targets also have no scroll-margin, so linked headings land under the sticky nav.
The “Read the manual (PDF)” link and most footer utility links point to `#` rather than a real destination.
The reservation confirmation is simulated UI feedback; it does not perform a reservation or email action.
Advertised mechanic not built: the alert and HUD claim a dash/burst on brake release; the update loop only multiplies speed by 0.42 while held.
Particle fade sets material.opacity on a MeshBasicMaterial created without transparent:true, so the opacity fade is inert — only the scale shrink actually reads.
hitFlash.style.background is permanently overwritten to the red death gradient on first hit and never restored, so subsequent near-miss flashes use the wrong colour.
Held keys are not cleared in resetWorld(), so input state can survive a restart, contrary to the brief.
Score bonus for passing an obstacle (+18) is gated on a userData.passed flag set in a branch that fires before the check, making that reward effectively dead logic.
`resetWorld()` does not reset `keys`, so held steering/brake input can survive death and immediately affect a new run, contrary to the brief's explicit restart-input requirement.

Particle materials are created without `transparent:true`, so setting `p.material.opacity` does not reliably produce the intended alpha fade; their scale fades, but the opacity mechanism is not correctly configured.

The play button explicitly switches audio from the initially muted state to audible. It is user-initiated and has a mute control, so this is not autoplay, but it is less conservative than keeping optional audio muted until the player opts in.
Tray previews are decorative only — the placed stone is a different randomly generated shape than the one shown, contradicting the on-screen promise that each stone is unique and clickable.
'Tide in' button is a no-op due to groundY being overwritten in buildGround().
Save-image comment claims a higher-resolution export path that was not built; export omits the CSS-drawn sky/background.
Three supplied screenshots are identical with the intro overlay still up (pointer delta 0), so the actual stacking state is never demonstrated.

The Tide In control does not retain a changed shoreline: it decrements `groundY`, then immediately calls `buildGround()`, which resets `groundY` to `H - 62`; its meaningful effect is just a small wind gust.
Reset repeatedly creates new Mouse instances and canvas/document event listeners without removing prior mouse listeners or explicitly disposing old constraints.
The Save Image feature exports only the physics canvas, not the composed interface, despite its broad label.
All three captured frames are identical with the blocking welcome overlay still up; interaction score 0 / mean pixel delta 0 — no screenshot evidence of stacking, physics, or wind actually running.

Fabricated identity: the page invents a product name ("Muse Spark") and attributes it to Meta, directly violating the brief's first requirement not to invent a product name or hide behind a persona. Every self-description that follows is therefore unverifiable fiction.

Claims "No fabricated stats on this page" and "No invented evidence" while simultaneously asserting "Latency: Fast", "Fidelity: High", "small, fast, cheap to run everywhere" and a training-cutoff/context-limit profile for a model that does not exist.
The demonstration is faked: hardcoded output blocks chosen by substring tests, marketed as "Live proof, not claims" and "verifiable now".
Fabricated product identity: “Muse Spark — Meta” is presented as a real specific model despite not being one.
The page repeatedly represents a handcrafted local regex/template generator as evidence of the claimed model’s behavior (“Try me live,” “Run Spark,” “Live proof”).

Unsupported factual product positioning is stated confidently throughout, including model size, latency/cost characteristics, tool-use behavior, structured-output fidelity, and comparative suitability.
User text is inserted into `outEl.innerHTML` without escaping, enabling HTML injection in the supposedly local demonstration.
Fabricated model/product identity (“Muse Spark by Meta”) — direct violation of accurate naming and no-fabrication rules
Automated identity check confirms it never names a specific real model
@media(prefers-contrast:more){--border:#000;--card:#fff} declares custom properties with no selector — invalid CSS that does nothing, so the claimed prefers-contrast support is not implemented.
validate() appends the error id to aria-describedby without dedup or removal, so repeated submissions accumulate duplicate ids and a stale error reference survives after the field is fixed.

role="radiogroup" sprayed onto a div that already wraps native radios inside a fieldset/legend, and aria-label on the non-interactive .logo div — redundant ARIA where the native element already did the job.
Seat grid rows contain an aria-hidden row-label span as a direct child of role="row", which is not a permitted child of a row in the grid pattern.

User-entered name and email values are interpolated into `innerHTML` for the review and confirmation content without escaping. Entering markup can alter the rendered review/confirmation DOM and its accessibility tree.
The code comments imply an Alt+Arrow row-skip feature, but the implementation is a no-op duplication of normal vertical movement.
Held-only orders are incorrectly charged carriage; saved quote totals for such orders can show £0.00 while loading the quote produces a nonzero carriage total.

The "96px display" step in both size ramps is rendered at width/height:68px with stroke-width forced to 1.4 — the page labels a size it does not actually show, and the brief specifically asks the set to hold at 96px.
Contradictory stated facts: the hero says "4.1 KB gzipped sprite", the hygiene checklist says "~6.2 KB / 1.9 KB gz".
The anemometer card claims a "three-cup hub" but only two cups are drawn in the symbol.
The dashboard's tide curve is a dashed empty box captioned "TIDE CURVE — 24H" — a placeholder in a deliverable that forbids placeholders.
The stated 96px size-ramp evidence is inaccurate: the markup uses 68px icons while labeling them 96px.
The “Hover to see code” claim is not implemented.
No-op paths in buoy and tide-gauge (broken authored geometry, not just sparse drawing)

Time-axis scale mismatch: label column (40px per half-hour) and cell/booking column (20px rows, percentage positioning over a container that includes the header) disagree, so displayed block times do not line up with the axis.
Empty-state copy tells the user to "drag the playhead" — there is no playhead and no click-to-create anywhere in the code.
Automated capture reports 0 fps and zero pixel delta after scripted pointer interaction; the three screenshots are identical, so no interactive change was observed.
The empty-state copy claims a nonexistent “playhead” can be dragged.
`window.addEventListener('resize',()=>{ if(drag) { /* cancel transform to avoid jump */ } });` does not cancel or recompute an active drag, leaving stale drag geometry after resize.
Automated interaction evidence reports zero pointer pixel movement; while source contains a drag implementation, the delivered interaction was not demonstrably exercised by the capture.
Filter interaction is non-functional: `:has()` filter selectors reference radios outside the `.catalog` subtree, so no card is ever hidden.
The sidebar "Reading position" indicator is faked — `.reading i::after{transform:scaleX(.35)}` is a static hardcoded 35% fill with no timeline or state driving it.
Several lightbox plates are effectively placeholders (a bare circle, a bare rounded rect), flagged in the source as "generic lightboxes for remaining cards (minimal)".
`@property --p` is dead code; `.catalog{container-type:inline-size}` has no corresponding container query.
No prohibited <script> tags, inline on* event attributes, or javascript: URLs were found.
Required filterable index is nonfunctional because the :has() selectors target inputs that are outside the .catalog subtree.
Filterable index does not filter—:has() scope bug makes the required interaction a no-op.
Faked reading-position indicator in the sticky TOC (static fill, not scroll-linked).
